pending.script: She checked into the Harrogate hotel as Teresa Neele. After an eleven-day search, the missing author was finally located. She had behaved in a modest, withdrawn manner among the guests. But the strangest part wasn't her disguise. Two examining doctors concluded she was suffering from total memory loss, cementing an official version the family maintained for decades. Agatha never spoke of those eleven days again, omitting them from her autobiography. Did she fake her memory loss, or was it a true psychological break? Comment below.

reasons: Factual and respectful presentation of a historical missing persons case without graphic violence, gore, or sensationalized victim trauma.

The script describes a well-documented historical disappearance where the individual involved (Agatha Christie) was not accused of any crime, and it avoids casting specific, actionable suspicion on her husband (Archie) or any other identifiable third party regarding criminal wrongdoing. It merely presents the known historical narrative and invites viewers to discuss theories regarding her psychological state ('memory loss' vs 'psychological break'), which is permissible as it does not accuse anyone of a crime.
